summary: Round 11 independent review: PASS with no findings. I recomputed both binding hashes myself (queueStore.ts=3638d31df6b133a2758d88b34bd081fd77551799e472811369da5409950e2af5, useImageGeneratorExecution.ts=6c417d98d3f29f250eb2af6971a5eaefb949d7e0d80988373aa465c56acbb4c2) and they match the candidate manifest exactly; HEAD=f86048863c6c2598697a17e43bcd7f8bc770e1b2, and src/ has exactly one modified file. Independent method for the comment-only claim: git diff HEAD -U0 -- src/ = 19 insertions / 4 deletions, 23 changed lines total, and filtering out every line whose content starts with // leaves the set EMPTY, while git diff HEAD --numstat -- src/ lists only queueStore.ts (the hook is byte-identical to HEAD). Round 9's claim is gone file-wide (all four literal fragments return zero hits in the file) and the corrected text at :1002 does agree with :947/:948. I re-ran the supplied exit probe in my own %TEMP% copy (single instance asserted, PASS 11/11, exit 0) and reproduced (a)=nopending/2 passes, (b)=nopending/3, (c)=cap/8 with 0/0/1 warnings. I then attacked the new text with a differently-built probe that counts REAL writes at the write sites inside clearNodeQueuedMarker rather than inferring them: claim :987 (the predicate writes nothing on legal marks) is confirmed by direct measurement - in the LEGAL shapes every flowStore write was on gen-x, zero on gen-legal, and there were zero canvasStore writes; claim :989 is confirmed (1 invocation, passes=2, exit=:948 !healPending, 0 warnings, X healed, LEGAL preserved, zero candidate-exit hits); claim :991 is confirmed (8 passes, exit=cap, exactly 1 warning, X residue true); and I swept the bounded writer N=1,2,3,6,7,8,9,12, reproducing the healing boundary N<=7 healed / N>=8 residue, with 0 warnings for N<=7 and 1 warning for N>=8. Functional spot-checks all pass on a forced single instance: F-R5-1 (5 rejected clicks => jobs stays 1, zero flowStore/canvasStore subscriber hits, node-data object identity unchanged, data.error and data.status untouched, and exactly 5 info toasts), REQ-002 (no concurrent duplicate job), F-R3-2 (a falsy marker produces zero canvasStore writes and no canvas identity change; my own triggering write is the only flowStore hit), F1 (stale marker cleared in BOTH carriers; negative control with a running job keeps both carriers true). Regression: 13/13 standing probes green (guard2 12/12, batch-chain 15/15, plus 11 clean RESULT lines), tsc --noEmit exit 0 with empty output. One factual inaccuracy I found is PRE-EXISTING HEAD text, unchanged by this candidate and therefore not a finding: :963 says N=7's exit is the zero-candidate path and :967 says passes = N+1, whereas I measure N=7 exiting at cap:p8 with passes 3,4,5,8,8,8 for N=1,2,3,6,7,8. The operative conclusions of those lines (N=7 is healed with zero warnings; N>=8 stays capped) are both confirmed.

Reproduced with my own harness, not inherited.

Final lines observed: probe-r4-guard2.mjs => summary PASS 12 / FAIL 0 (of 12); probe-batch-chain.mjs => 15/15 pass; probe-cross-canvas.mjs => the two canvases do not interfere; probe-req001-coldstart.mjs => node usable, REQ-001 fixed; probe-cancel-abort-lock.mjs => no permanent lock formed; probe-reject-timeline.mjs => inconsistency not captured; probe-reject-erases-marker.mjs => marker consistent with active jobs, not reproduced; probe-r3-stranded-canvas-copy.mjs => not reproduced, all carriers reset when the nodeId has no active job; probe-lock-via-ui.mjs => no permanent lock, marker cleared by the following job; probe-r3-erased-while-queued-paused.mjs => not reproduced; probe-r3-finally-churn.mjs => the App.tsx:170-equivalent subscribe hit count is 0 (the required zero-subscribe-hit property); probe-r4-undo-restart.mjs with R4_PHASE=restart => not reproduced (after restart the canvas copy is queued=false, canRun true, recoverable job count 0); probe-r4-undo-cancel.mjs after the documented fixture fix (the missing third data argument on addNode) => runtime not reproduced, with marker true and button disabled after the paused click, marker false after cancel, marker false with 0 active jobs after Ctrl+Z, and the canvas copy queued=false. I did NOT run scripts/queue-regression.mjs because it creates scripts/.nc-mutants-* temporary directories inside the repository and this review is read-only; for the gate I cite the recorded non-empty capture (4571 bytes) together with my own tsc run and the 13 green probes above, so no check was left NOT_RUN. Note on evidence hygiene: the round-10 narrative mentions a probe-r10-newtext.mjs, but no such file exists anywhere under the evidence tree (review-probes-r10 contains probe-r9-exits.mjs, r10-validate.mjs and unrelated UI/CDP harnesses), so that specific artifact could not be re-executed and I substituted my own constructed attacks.

Attack on the new comment text, looking for a necessity claim the code does not guarantee. The two absolute words in the corrected block are at :978 (the candidates.length === 0 branch can never be hit) and :1002 (reaching here necessarily means this round had a nested write). Both survive falsification. (i) :978 follows from collectQueuedMarkerCandidates judging on marker === true while the predicate deliberately preserves legal marks (:931-932): my instrumentation of the :922 early return fired zero times (zeroTop=0) across every LEGAL shape, including the unbounded re-arm writer. (ii) :1002 is a re-entrancy consequence: reaching :995 requires !healPending to have been false at :948, and healPending is only set by the re-entry guard at :913-915 (set the flag and return), which is reached only from the flowStore subscription firing inside a nodes write. I searched for a zero-nested-write counterexample with my own probe that tags all four exit sites plus the top-level early return; every shape that reached the cap had a nested write (cap:p8 always, with 8 predicate writes), and every zero-nested-write shape exited at :948 with nopending, so the classification holds. (iii) The three inlined numbers all reproduce with real-write instrumentation: (a) 1 invocation, passes=2, exit nopending at :948, flowStore writes=1 (on gen-x), canvasStore writes=0, warnings=0, X=false, LEGAL=true; (b) 1 invocation, passes=8, exit cap, flowStore writes=8 (all on gen-x), canvasStore writes=0, warnings=1, X=true; (c) the N sweep giving HEALED for N<=7 with 0 warnings and RESIDUE for N>=8 with 1 warning. (iv) :987's supporting claim (the predicate writes nothing at all on legal marks in that round) is directly measured rather than inferred: instrumenting the real flowStore.updateNodeData call site inside clearNodeQueuedMarker shows every write was on gen-x and none on gen-legal, with canvasStore writes=0 in all LEGAL shapes. (v) :1009's claim that the break below runs unconditionally and that termination never depends on the read-only criterion is literally true (:1026 break; sits outside the if (stillClearable > 0) block), and stillClearable being read-only is consistent with the absence of any additional subscriber hit at the cap. F-R5-2 (a third-party subscriber that re-introduces a stale true during the heal) is also still closed: the measured nodes-array sequence shows gen-x:true re-armed by the writer and then cleared again on the following pass, which is exactly the deferred-not-dropped behaviour :849 requires. KNOWN PRE-EXISTING INACCURACY, NOT A FINDING: :963 states that N=7 rescanned 8 times and that the exit is the zero-candidate path, whereas I measure exit cap:p8 for N=7 (the :954 zero-candidate check did run and found nothing, but the exit actually taken is the cap at :995, which is precisely why the warning is suppressed by stillClearable=0); :967-968's 'passes = N+1' likewise measures 3,4,5 for N=1,2,3 and 8 for both N=6 and N=7 instead of 2,3,4,7,8. Both sentences are byte-identical to HEAD (git show HEAD:src/stores/queueStore.ts contains the same corrected-N=7 sentence), neither appears anywhere in this candidate's diff, and the operative claims they support (N=7 is healed with zero warnings; N>=8 stays capped with a residue) are both confirmed - so they do not falsify the change under review, but they are inaccurate and should not be cited as exact exit-path evidence in future rounds.

The change is comment-only, so it cannot alter behaviour, and it strictly improves accuracy: it removes an assertion that was measurably wrong (the claim that the exit necessarily falls through to the cap) and replaces it with a two-branch statement both of whose branches I reproduced, adding in-line that round 9 found the error and that the text was corrected. Cross-references introduced by the new text are correct: the new block points at :947 for the !healPending hit condition, :947's own comment (this line is hit only when this round had no nested write at all) is consistent with it, and :1002's parenthetical repeats that pointer. The write-loop hazard documentation at :848-871 remains consistent with the code: healingQueuedMarkers only defers (:913-915 sets healPending and returns), the flag is cleared in the finally block, and MAX_HEAL_PASSES = 8 at :893 still bounds the synchronous stack. Two wording concerns are recorded for completeness and do not block: (1) the pre-existing zero-candidate exit phrase at :963 described above; (2) the absolute word at :978 is safe only because collectQueuedMarkerCandidates is unchanged and the predicate's legal-mark preservation is intentional, so a future change to either would silently invalidate it - the sentence does tie itself to :931-932, which mitigates this. Neither is a defect in this candidate, being respectively pre-existing and correctly scoped.

The synchronous-stack cost claims (8 passes are only 8 small scans in one synchronous stack, measured at the 1ms scale, and exiting within 0-1ms) are pre-existing text, but the bounding behaviour they rely on is re-verified here: with the unbounded re-arm writer the loop performed exactly 8 passes and 8 predicate writes and then stopped, so the synchronous stack is bounded at 8 iterations no matter how often the writer re-arms; the N sweep shows N=9 and N=12 also stop at 8 passes with 8 writes, so an unbounded writer cannot extend the stack (the round-5 precedent of 200000+ writes over about 3.5 seconds is closed by the cap, whose numeric value this candidate leaves unchanged). The cheap no-op path is confirmed too: for a falsy marker the heal produces zero canvasStore writes, zero canvas identity change, and no writes of its own to flowStore (my triggering write was the only subscriber hit), so the 800ms debounce -> updateCanvasData -> persist chain documented at :586-592 is not triggered by healing. The 8-pass cap still leaves the documented N>=8 residue, which is an accepted and honestly recorded trade-off (a bounded synchronous stack is preferred over an unbounded one), not a performance regression. No new performance surface is introduced because the diff adds no executable line.
